Figure 1:Overview of SkeLAM.(A) Skeleton supervision and cross-modal swap reconstruction structure RGB transition latents into kinematic and residual components.
(B) Separate projections condition the world model: keep retains both branches, partial drops one, and null drops both.
(C) An action adapter predicts kinematic latents, with the null residual at inference.

Figure 2:Skeleton-grounded latent action learning.(A) RGB and skeleton transition encoding.
(B) Grounding through a frozen skeleton decoder.
(C) Swap reconstruction using the paired skeleton mean and the same RGB residual sample.

Figure 3:Qualitative comparison of action-conditioned world modeling.Ground-truth and generated observations are compared at selected time steps, highlighting differences in end-effector motion, manipulated-object geometry, and scene appearance.

Figure 5:Zero-shot human-to-robot motion transfer.Human videos from UniSkill(Kim et al., 2025)provide latent conditions for robot rollout generation.
Markers indicate end-effector positions.

Figure 8:Tabletop scene.Columns: ground truth, SkeLAM, DreamDojo, Cosmos-Predict2.5, OSCAR, and Ctrl-World.
Rows:TT,T+4T+4,T+8T+8, andT+12T+12.
Colored markers and arrows highlight end-effector motion in the final row.
